answer: The three words are derived from a 69 bit value mixing the epoch seed with the identity key, so no two keys ever receive the same triple. Because the bridge nonce is published only after close, the ember audit can verify each derivation and a shared text is provable as copied. That removes the entire premise of a template farm, which depends on one text serving many identities, and forces a separate glacier derivation per key. That is 31 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
